title: Has anyone here made a multiplayer game? What was the process / outcome?
author: No_Departure7494
selftext:
Anytime I ask claude to consider making my game multiplayer it warns me "This shit gonna be fuckin' tough little man so buckle up".

I don't know many people with gaming PCs to even test it with so I kept it singleplayer.

comments.author: Masterkiefs
comments.body: Multiplayer and co op I’m such a big fan of, so it was a mandatory for me, the games built around it and it brings extra fun!

replies.author: Masterkiefs
replies.body: It’s still playable solo tho, if you do have trouble finding someone. Best of both worlds. It all depends on the game too

replies.author: No_Departure7494
replies.body: Did you consider it from the jump? That's what it said in my prompt. That if you're gonna aim for multiplayer, start that way. Don't try to crowbar it in later.

replies.author: Masterkiefs
replies.body: Yes I did, it’s one of the early part of the builds for me. You can use steams online services or epic games, to help with the multiplayer. Then you wanna make sure the netcode is good in sync. I am sure you could ask to have it plan it for you and what that would look like, pros and cons, etc. then cross review it with another model to see if can kill the idea

comments.author: Hfcsmakesmefart
comments.body: lol, codex did it in half a day with Unity. Even made every move atomic and did checks against grifters.

replies.author: Living_Cell7304
replies.body:
Made every move atomic? Wtf does that mean?  
Are you talking about multi threading on their job system?

And unless your server is also running the simulation and only accepting inputs from the clients, it’s going to be open to cheating - no matter what “checks” you’re doing

replies.author: theflossboss1
replies.body: Can you explain what you mean by “every move atomic”?  That is usually not the right term to describe multiplayer movement

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body: Making multiplayer isn't hard if you go into the game understanding that's the plan. Specifically... it's not hard if you don't care about people hacking in the game. If you're just making a casual game for friends to play with friends, you don't need to worry so much about whether a server or player's computer is handling certain calculations, so you can focus on whichever is most efficient. But for competitive games you have to start either making things server authoritative or having all players' PCs in the game check against each other (so the majority can hold random anomalies accountable.) I opted to just assume that, for my game, people are only playing it with friends that they trust enough not to try and spoof packets (the game has plenty of systems that would be broken by players who don't want other people to have fun, anyway.)

comments.author: Will_X_Intent
comments.body: If you design the game with multiplayer in mind, it shouldnt be hard.  Replication and all that.

comments.author: Toastti
comments.body:
Your biggest mistake is trying to add multiplayer later in the games development lifecycle. You absolutely have to start your game with multiplayer in mind from the very very beginning 


You really want to have some networking and programming experience on your own before you jump into making a multiplayer game. Once you start having to think about what is client owned versus server owned, how you will send updates to every online player performantly etc you will run into real issues if you don't have that experience

comments.author: SomnambulisticTaco
comments.body:
Try rebuilding an abandoned game, get the feel for how everything goes together.

Grav, for example. I always liked it but devs ruined and abandoned it.

Now I’ve got non steam local multiplayer including the steamdeck. It’s a learning process, and the next thing I do will be better.

comments.author: Chocoweb88
comments.body:
I've made an android card game with multiplayer pvp elements, and there's Ranked Match and leaderboard too. Unity has most of the tools and plugins for free. I used Photon Pun 2 to establish room connection.  It is free but can only hold i think 20 concurrent users, but it works well as i test play it between me and my test phones.

The issue is... I cant get players to test play my game lol. So I never tested the real capacity of the multiplayers aspect.

Claude also said it implemented anti cheating function, though im not sure how it works and if it works lol. Need real players/hackers to test it for me

comments.author: Limp-Caterpillar8661
comments.body: I have a space mmo game with 1 player and use cloudflare

comments.author: WhiteBlackBlueGreen
comments.body: Im honestly a bit afraid to test the implementation because of potential cybersecurity mishaps
